models.section: 4.2 The Price Prediction Model Based on LSTM
models.purpose: Forecast the next day's gold price and bitcoin price from a window of past prices.
models.summary: A standard LSTM with the three usual gates, fed by a sliding window, tuned one parameter at a time against MAPE.

equation_status.reason: visually checked against crops; subscripts confirmed on the page

objectives: Choose the hyperparameter combination with the smallest MAPE.
constraints: The first 14 days are skipped because the training window is too small.
One hyperparameter moves at a time; the other four stay at their initial values.

details: The first 14 days are skipped because the training window is too small, stated in the assumptions.
No spatial boundary; the model runs over trading days.

parameter_estimation.method: Five hyperparameters adjusted one at a time, the other four held fixed, choosing the smallest MAPE. Table 3 bolds the minimum of each column, and each bold minimum is the initial value.

steps: Take the previous d days as the input window.
Train each day on its previous d' days, with d' < d.
Stop when the time limit is reached.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: until the time limit is reached; no numerical tolerance is given

assumptions: Prices are a time series, so a sequential model is appropriate.
One parameter can be judged while the others stay at their initial values.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Not discussed. The introduction names vanishing and exploding gradients as the reason for choosing LSTM, and no gradient check is reported.

validation_refs: Figure 4 overlays predicted and real curves and the text says the model is proven good by comparing them. No number is attached at that point.
The MAPE values 0.007261 and 0.041630 appear in the summary, not beside the formula.
strengths: Each gate is introduced with the same sentence, so the reader can compare them.
The tuning rule is stated before the scan.
limitations: MAPE is written with the gold price only. The text says both assets are judged under the same parameter combination, but no bitcoin MAPE formula is displayed.
The scan never leaves the initial values.
missing_details: how n in MAPE is counted

data_provenance.source: LBMA gold and the bitcoin series supplied by COMAP
data_provenance.cleaning: Ten missing gold trading days filled by the average of the neighboring days, Table 2.
data_provenance.leakage_risk: The fill uses the following day's price. The paper does not say whether a filled value is ever used as an input to a decision made before that day. Open.

source_notes.assumption_consequence: If the best value of one parameter depends on another, the one-at-a-time scan misses it. The bold minima landing on the initial values is consistent with that miss, not proof of it.
source_notes.numerical_stability: The introduction of LSTM names vanishing and exploding gradients as the reason for the choice. No gradient check is reported.
source_notes.validation_scope: A curve overlay can show shape agreement. It cannot show that the forecast is usable for trading, because it is not scored against a naive forecast here.
source_notes.result_translation: model output -> Figure 4 overlay -> 'proven to be good by comparing the predicted curve and the real curve' -> the strategy is allowed to use the forecast -> no caveat at the handoff

base_modification_contract.base_mechanism: LSTM with forget, input and output gates
base_modification_contract.paper_modification: sliding window with two lengths, d for input and d' for training, and one-at-a-time hyperparameter search on MAPE
base_modification_contract.claimed_benefit: best prediction result under a shared parameter combination
base_modification_contract.evidence_of_benefit: Table 3, whose bold minima are the starting values
base_modification_contract.transfer_boundary: The one-at-a-time search is only reasonable when parameters do not interact.

source_notes.reproduction_status: not reproducible: optimizer, seed and software absent

models.section: 4.3 Investment Strategy Model Based on MLP
models.family: multi-objective linear program solved by ideal point
models.purpose: Turn tomorrow's predicted prices into a buy and sell decision that raises return and lowers risk.
models.summary: Risk and return defined on the traded amounts, cash in neither, the two objectives rewritten as a single minimization, then split into six programs by the sign pattern of the trade.

governing_equations.source_expression: x'_c = x_c - delta x_g - delta x_b
predicted worth after the trade < predicted worth of holding
governing_equations.normalized_latex: x'_c + \frac{\hat{r}_{g,t+1}}{r_{g,t}} x'_g + \frac{\hat{r}_{b,t+1}}{r_{b,t}} x'_b < x_c + \frac{\hat{r}_{g,t+1}}{r_{g,t}} x_g + \frac{\hat{r}_{b,t+1}}{r_{b,t}} x_b
governing_equations.purpose: Do nothing when the best trade is worth less than holding. Both sides use predicted prices; the prose calls both 'return value'.

equation_status.reason: visually checked. The risk statistic divides by 9 and sums 10 terms: the sample standard deviation, printed exactly that way.

objectives: Printed first as max P, min R.
Rewritten on the next page as min -P, R.
constraints: A buy cannot spend more cash than is held.
A sell cannot exceed the holding after commission: -delta x < (1 - alpha) x.
On a day gold does not trade, delta x_g = 0.

details: [1000, 0, 0] on September 25, 2016, after the first 14 days are skipped
No spatial boundary; the model runs over trading days.

parameter_estimation.method: No parameter is estimated. The commissions are given by the problem and the risk window of 10 is chosen and never varied.

steps: On a gold trading day run behaviors i to iv.
On a non-trading day run behaviors v and vi. The closing paragraph prints this range as v-iv, backwards.
Compare the best program against doing nothing through (13).
algorithm.convergence_criteria: The ideal-point step; no tolerance and no solver software are named.

assumptions: No minimum purchase lot, because the starting capital cannot buy one ounce.
Commission does not move the market price, assumed because the sensitivity task needs it.
Intraday prices collapse to one value, because the problem gives nothing finer.
Dollar inflation is ignored, because the problem does not give it.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Cash cannot go negative and a sell cannot exceed the holding, both written as constraints. No infeasibility case is discussed, and P and R are never rescaled before the squaring.

validation_refs: Section 5 compares against four declared rivals on ten metrics.
strengths: The naive all-in bitcoin rule is written out and then rejected before the model is built.
Six behaviors share one three-sentence template, so the sign pattern is the only thing the reader must track.
limitations: Cash earns neither return nor risk, so holding cash is free.
The ideal point needs the separate optima omega_i, and the paper does not say how those are computed for this problem.
missing_details: how the individual optima are obtained
whether P and R are scaled before squaring

data_provenance.source: predicted prices from MU-01 and the realized prices up to day t
data_provenance.coverage: the same span as the forecast
data_provenance.transformation: gold priced per troy ounce, bitcoin per coin, both in US dollars
data_provenance.leakage_risk: P uses r-hat for tomorrow and r for today. The risk statistic uses the 10 prices before day t. No future price enters the decision except through the forecast, which is the point of the model.

source_notes.assumption_consequence: If the commission did move the price, the sensitivity sweep would measure the wrong thing. The paper states this and assumes it away.
source_notes.numerical_stability: Not discussed. The ideal point step squares the distance to the separate optima, so the scale of P and of R matters, and the paper never rescales either.
source_notes.validation_scope: The rival comparison shows the strategy beats the rivals it names. It does not show the strategy is the best possible, because the ideal foresight row in Table 4 is not part of the argument.
source_notes.result_translation: daily portfolio -> Figures 5 and 6 -> 'The result is' sentence -> the terminal value in the summary -> the memorandum's annualized rate -> the letter concedes the result is daily and two-asset only

base_modification_contract.base_mechanism: multi-objective linear programming reduced by the ideal point method
base_modification_contract.paper_modification: six sign-pattern cases, cash excluded from both objectives, and a do-nothing test above all six
base_modification_contract.claimed_benefit: a daily strategy that balances return and risk
base_modification_contract.interface: consumes the two predicted prices, emits the portfolio
base_modification_contract.transfer_boundary: The case split assumes exactly two assets with one of them sometimes untradable.

source_notes.reproduction_status: partially specified: the programs are written, the solver is not

dependency_edges.handoff: predicted gold price and predicted bitcoin price for day t+1, in US dollars per ounce and per coin, used as r-hat in the return P and in the do-nothing test (13); not used in the risk statistic, which takes realized prices

printed_defects_retained: (4) is introduced with 'show in equation (4)', not 'shown'.
The input gate paragraph says the output lies 'between 0 1', the word 'and' missing.
MAPE in (8) carries only the gold price. Bitcoin's MAPE is quoted in the summary and never written as a formula.
The risk statistic divides by 9 and sums 10 terms. Kept as printed.
The objective is printed as 'max P, min R' and rewritten as 'min -P, R' with no comma spacing.
The non-trading-day range is printed 'model v-iv', backwards.
(13) compares predicted worth against predicted worth, so it never uses the realized price. The prose calls both sides 'return value'.
The closing result sentence drops its verb: 'worth' stands where 'is worth' would.
transcription_note: Every displayed equation below was read from a cropped page proxy, not from the text layer. The text layer drops subscripts and fraction bars. Printed wording is kept even where the grammar slips.
